newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/End of Conrail saga seen near.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/End of Conrail saga seen near.

text.p: Conrail Inc options continued active on the Philadelphia Stock Exchange (PHLX) Tuesday as investors bet on a conclusion to the company's takeover saga by the November expiration, traders said.
"The assumption the market is making is that there will be big news before November" expiration, one trader said. "So the November volatilities are a lot higher than the December volatilities."
Conrail November 95 and 100 calls were trading with a volatility of 34 Tuesday while the comparable December calls were trading with volatilities in the low 20s.
November options expire on November 15.
"There's pretty good volume on the call side in November and December," one trader said. "Not a lot in the puts."
Last month, Conrail agreed to be bought by CSX Corp for $92.50 a share in stock and cash in a deal that valued Conrail at $8.4 billion.
But Norfolk Southern Corp later countered with an all-cash $100 a share offer.
On Tuesday, Norfolk Southern said it filed a definitive proxy statement with regulators seeking to block Conrail's plan to amend its company articles.
Norfolk said it had received signed commitments from banks for more than $15 billion to fund its proposed offer.
Norfolk shares were down 1-5/8 at 89-1/8 Tuesday afternoon and CSX shares were down 7/8 at 44.
Options traders said the market was split evenly between the two offers. Conrail shares were down one at 92-5/8 Tuesday afternoon.
Among the options, the November 95 call was most active, with about 3,400 contracts changing hands. The option was down 1/16 at 1-7/16. Its open interest was about 7,100 contracts.
The November 100 call traded 2,735 contracts, about all of its open interest. The contract was unchanged at 3/4.
In the December series, the 90 call traded 1,800 contracts, the 95 call traded 2,320 and the 100 call traded 1,205.
The December 100 calls were trading down 1/16 at 11/16.
One trader said the low premium for that option suggested investors see little chance the stock will break through that 100 level.
The January 100 call traded 210 contracts. It was down 1/8 at 1-1/8 and had open interest of about 1,855 contracts.
The most active Conrail put was the November 90, which traded 1,070 contracts. The option rose 1/16 to 1-3/8. Its open interest was about 3,430, which included an addition of 1,600 contracts Monday.
"The market is saying there's zero chance of a third bid" for Conrail, a trader said, referring to the recent options activity.
